text: Two extracts, two real T-SQL queries, built straight against AdventureWorks2012.

The customer-segment extract joins Sales dot Customer to order data, and builds the segment label right in SQL with a CASE expression: StoreID populated means Store slash Reseller, otherwise Individual. Status equals 5 restricts both extracts to shipped, completed orders.
The territory extract joins the same order data through Sales dot SalesTerritory instead, pulling TerritoryName and TerritoryGroup alongside SalesOrderID, OrderDate, and LineTotal.

Both extracts come out bigger than you might expect, because joining in SalesOrderDetail causes row fan-out: one row per order line, repeating the header columns. That's expected for a line-level extract, since the actual dollar amount lives on SalesOrderDetail, not the header.
Next lesson profiles these two extracts side by side and finds exactly what's wrong once someone tries to combine them.
